text.p: Swedish drugs group Astra said on Monday German rival Altana AG's decision to suspend the clinical development of a successor to its anti-ulcer agent Pantoprazol should strengthen Astra's position longterm.

"In the long term this could not mean anything else than Astra's position on the market will strengthen compared to (its position) if the (Panotprazol) successor had been launched," Astra spokesman Staffan Ternby told Reuters.
Altana said on Monday it suspended the clinical development of Pumazol, a successor to Pantaprazol.
Astra's largest drug is anti-ulcer agent Losec.
Sales of Pantoprazol amounted to about two billion crowns in 1996 while Losec sales totalled 25 billion crowns, Ternby said.
"Altana's decision doesn't mean a dramatic change of our future prospects. But it is always sad when late phase research projects have to be broken off," Ternby said.
Pumazol was a short acting, or reversible, version of Pantoprazol and Astra expects to present a short acting acid pump inhibitor sometime after the year 2000.
"Astra has come the furthest with a successor to Losec, which we expect to be able to present around the turn of the century. Work with the agent looks good," Ternby said.
"Our work with a short acting acid-pump inhibitor is in an early phase. Such an agent will come to the market at the earliest after the year 2000, if we succeed with it," he said.
Currently, no short acting acid pump inhibitors are on the market, Ternby said.
